title: The Broken Crayon
moral: Forgiveness makes room for love. Sometimes a broken thing can help repair a hurt heart.

pages.text:
Aarav's little sister, Mini, loved colouring.

She coloured trees purple, suns green, and once gave a fish big red shoes.

"Fish do not wear shoes," Aarav said.

Mini looked serious. "This one does."

Aarav had a new box of crayons. It had twenty-four colours, all sharp and perfect. His favourite was sky blue.

On Sunday afternoon, he was drawing a big ocean for his school chart. He left the crayons on the table and went to drink water.

When he came back, Mini was holding the sky-blue crayon.

It was broken in two.

Aarav's face became hot.

"Mini! That was my best crayon!"

Mini's lips trembled. "I was making clouds."

"Clouds are not blue!" Aarav said.

Mini looked at her paper. "Mine are."

Aarav took the broken pieces and walked away. He did not speak to her for the rest of the afternoon.

Later, he saw Mini sitting quietly near the window. Her paper was folded in half.

Their mother came and looked at Aarav's chart.

"The ocean looks nice," she said. "But where is the sky?"

Aarav looked at the broken crayon in his hand.

He could still use it.

Slowly, he went to Mini.

"Show me your clouds," he said.

Mini opened the paper.

She had drawn two blue clouds and one tiny boat under them. In the boat were two stick people.

"This is you and me," she said. "The blue clouds are keeping us cool."

Aarav's anger became very small.

He sat beside her.

"I shouted," he said. "I am sorry."

Mini gave him one broken piece. "You can have big half."

Aarav smiled. "Thank you."

Together, they coloured the sky on his chart. The broken crayon made thick, soft lines.

When the chart was done, Aarav wrote at the bottom: Ocean and Sky by Aarav and Mini.

Mini touched her name and smiled as if it were a prize. The crayon was broken, but the picture had become better because they shared it.
